import mir_eval
import numpy as np

# Adjust estimated intervals to match reference boundaries
est_intervals_adj, est_labels_adj = mir_eval.util.adjust_intervals(
    est_intervals, est_labels, 
    ref_intervals.min(), ref_intervals.max(), 
    mir_eval.chord.NO_CHORD, mir_eval.chord.NO_CHORD
)

# Merge intervals to create perfectly aligned label lists of equal length
intervals, merged_ref_labels, merged_est_labels = mir_eval.util.merge_labeled_intervals(
    ref_intervals, ref_labels, est_intervals_adj, est_labels_adj
)

# Compute MIREX scores on the aligned label lists
comparisons = mir_eval.chord.mirex(merged_ref_labels, merged_est_labels)

# Verify the result
assert isinstance(comparisons, np.ndarray), "Output must be a numpy array"
assert comparisons.shape == (len(merged_ref_labels),), "Output shape must match the number of aligned labels"
assert np.all((comparisons >= 0.0) & (comparisons <= 1.0)), "Scores must be in [0.0, 1.0]"

print(f"__CHECK__ mirex {comparisons.shape[0]},{comparisons.sum():.2f}")
